ig_carousel_topic.topic: CLV (closing line value) and why sharps obsess over it
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Why sharps don't care if they won.
They care what the line did after they bet it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors check the scoreboard.
Sharps check the closing line.
If the line moved against your bet, you probably got the worst of it, even if you won.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: The closing line is the most efficient price the market produces. Books and sharp syndicates have had maximum time to correct it. Beating it consistently means you found real value, not just a result.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
You bet a team at +145. It closes at +118.
The market moved 27 cents toward your side.
That's positive CLV. Over hundreds of bets, positive CLV predicts long-term profit better than your current win rate does.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: A 54% win rate with negative CLV is fragile. A 51% win rate with consistent positive CLV is a process worth trusting. The score tells you what happened. The closing line tells you if you're doing it right.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: CLV is the closest thing to a process check in sports betting. If you're not tracking it, you're missing half the picture.
